title: SVG drawings (.svg)
summary: A common subset of SVG, drawn sharply at the target size. An image can embed a picture, a model, a chart, or another SVG file that sits in the same folder.

items.text: Shapes: rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, path.
Grouping with g and cascading presentation attributes; transform; use and symbol; marker.
Linear and radial gradients (with href inheritance), pattern, clipPath, and mask.

Filters: the fe* primitives blend, color matrix, component transfer, composite, convolve matrix, lighting, displacement map, drop shadow, flood, Gaussian blur, image, merge, morphology, offset, tile, and turbulence.
image elements with a base64 data: URI in a supported raster format (an SVG given as a data: URI is not drawn); image-rendering selects smooth or pixelated drawing.

image elements with a relative href to a file in the folder of the SVG file or below it: a raster, an SVG file, an OpenSCAD model (.scad), a Vega-Lite chart (.vl.json), or a page of a PDF, PPTX, or VSDX document (page 1 unless the href ends in #page=N). The format is decided by the file name. A model or chart is drawn at the size of the image, a raster at its own size and then fitted; a file: URI inside the folder and a percent-encoded path also work, and a nested SVG file finds its own images beside itself.

An embedded model is drawn with the view the library chooses for it (isometric for a 3D model, top-down for a flat 2D model, or the model's own $vpr, $vpt, $vpd, and $vpf variables) over a transparent background, so the diagram shows through; an embedded chart keeps its own background (white unless it names another).
text, best effort, with weight and style: an installed family is used; the generic families and unknown families use the bundled Liberation Sans, Serif, and Mono.
The root viewBox and preserveAspectRatio (all aligns, meet and slice), and percent lengths.

CSS length units wherever SVG takes a length (shape and text positions and sizes, stroke-width, stroke-dasharray, stroke-dashoffset, font-size, gradient, pattern, and mask coordinates, and the root width and height): px, pt, pc, in, cm, mm, Q (1in is 96 user units), em, ex, ch, rem, lh, rlh, vw, vh, vmin, and vmax, in any letter case; a number without a unit is in user units. Also calc(), min(), max(), and clamp() with + - * / and nested parentheses; a math result keeps its type, so one that resolves to a plain number (such as calc(1 + 1)) is not a length (it is valid only for line-height, as a multiplier, and for objectBoundingBox gradient, pattern, and mask coordinates).

font-size from an attribute, a style attribute, a style element, or the font shorthand (style, weight, size, / line-height, family): lengths, percent, the keywords xx-small to xxx-large (9, 10, 13, 16, 18, 24, 32, and 48 pixels), larger and smaller (1.2 times), and inherit, initial, and unset. The keywords inherit, initial, and unset (alone as the font value, or on font-family, font-weight, and font-style) reset every font property including font-family. font-weight and font-style keywords are accepted in any letter case, and font-style takes oblique with an angle in deg, grad, rad, or turn (within 90deg either way). A font-family list splits only at commas outside quotes, so a quoted name can contain a comma. The first dx and dy of a text element move it.
CSS in a style element (type, class, id, universal, and compound selectors; descendant and child combinators; specificity) and inline style.
The intrinsic size is the viewBox, else width and height (converted from their units to user units), else 300x150.

An image element may link a file whose name ends in .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .bmp, .tif, .tiff, .gif, .jp2, .j2k, or .j2c (a raster picture), .svg (another SVG file), .scad (an OpenSCAD model), .vl.json or .vl (a Vega-Lite chart), or .pdf, .pptx, or .vsdx (a page of a document: a PDF page, a PowerPoint slide, or a Visio page; page 1 unless the href chooses another one, see page fragment below). The format is decided by the file name, not by the content, so a Vega-Lite chart in a file whose extension is only json is not linked; a raster file is still decoded by its content. Any other file is not drawn.

A model, a chart, a document page, and an SVG file are drawn at the size of the image element (its width and height on the output), so they stay sharp at any scale; a raster is fitted into the element by preserveAspectRatio. An embedded model uses the library's own view of the model (isometric for a 3D model, top-down for a flat 2D model) over a transparent background.

The href is relative to the folder of the SVG file (a nested SVG file finds its own images beside itself). A query (?cache=1) after the file name is ignored; a fragment (#page=2) after it is read as parameters, see page fragment below; an encoded %23 or %3F is a literal # or ? in the name. An absolute path, a drive letter, a path that leaves the folder with .., a symbolic link, and a network URL are never followed.

A fragment after the file name is a list of name=value parameters separated by & (RFC 8118 style: report.pdf#page=3). Names are not case sensitive, the first = of a parameter splits name from value, and %XX escapes are decoded after the split. Documents: pdf and vsdx take page=N, pptx takes page=N or slide=N (the same slide); N counts from 1 (digits only, leading zeros allowed), and with no parameter page 1 is drawn. A model takes view=iso|front|back|left|right|top|bottom instead of its automatic view. A raster and an SVG file take no parameter. A model and a chart also take the prefixed parameters of variable fragment below. If a name is given twice with different values the last one wins, with a warning. A fragment is at most {{fragmentMaxLength}} characters and {{fragmentMaxParameters}} parameters.

A model and a chart take parameters whose name starts with a prefix, so they never collide with the names above. A model: def.<name>=<value> sets the variable <name> of the model exactly like -D name=value of the command line (a number, true, false, or text; one pair of quotes is removed; a vector is a JSON array such as def.$vpt=[0,0,20]; the assignment of the file is replaced), for example part.scad#view=front&def.width=20&def.label=%22A%22 (%22 is a double quote). The viewport variables work too: def.$vpd=300 fixes the camera distance (and with it the scale), def.$vpt=[x,y,z] the target, def.$vpr=[a,b,c] the rotation, and def.$vpf the field of view, so several links of one model can share a scale. A chart: param.<name>=<value> sets the param <name> of the chart like --param, with the value true, false, null, a number, text, or JSON (a selection takes its initial state, for example chart.vl.json#param.threshold=5&param.brush={%22x%22:[2,6]}). The prefix is not case sensitive, the name after it is (as written), the value is decoded after the fragment is split, and the last value of a name wins. A value that is not usable (a def. name that is not an identifier, malformed JSON) is image-fragment-invalid and the image is not drawn; a param. name the chart does not declare is the warning vl-param-unknown and the chart is drawn without it. def. on anything but a model, and param. on anything but a chart, is image-fragment-unknown-parameter. A def. name the model does not assign creates the variable, as -D does.

An input path of the command line takes the same fragment: canvasnet render "report.pdf#page=3" -o p3.png, canvasnet render "chart.vl.json#param.t=5" -o c.png, canvasnet montage "part.scad#def.explode=0" "part.scad#def.explode=1" --labels -o m.png, canvasnet compare "a.scad#view=top" "b.scad#view=top". It works for render and its verbs, inspect, info, compare, and montage, with the same parameters and values as a link, and it overrides --page, --view, -D, and --param for that input (a variable or a param by name; the --azimuth, --elevation, and --projection of the command still refine the view). The # starts a fragment only when no file has that exact name (a file called chart#2.png keeps working); when the name before the # is a file, the longest such name is used. Quote the input in a shell: an & ends a command (bash, zsh) or is reserved (PowerShell), so "part.scad#view=top&def.width=20" needs quotes; a # at the start of a word begins a comment in bash. A value that cannot be used (the same cases as image-fragment-invalid above) is an error with the code image-fragment-invalid, and a page the file does not have is page-out-of-range; an unknown or repeated parameter name (image-fragment-unknown-parameter, image-fragment-duplicate-parameter, vl-param-unknown) is a warning, also with --strict, as for a link. Labels of montage show the fragment.

<image href="report.pdf#page=2" .../> draws the second page of the PDF file; <image href="deck.pptx#slide=3" .../> draws the third slide; <image href="drawing.vsdx#page=2" .../> the second page; <image href="part.scad#view=front" .../> the front view of a model. Inside an XML attribute a second parameter is written with &, for example report.pdf#page=2&page=3. Print a whole diagram with: canvasnet help svg --example embed-pages

A parameter the linked file does not use is not an error: the picture is drawn without it and the warning image-fragment-unknown-parameter is reported. This includes a fragment on a file that takes none, such as logo.png#anything or other.svg#top; such a link used to be ignored without a word.

A model linked from an image element follows the same rule as canvasnet render: a missing include or use file, a file outside the model's folder, or a circular include is a scad-error, so the image is not drawn and the render fails, naming the link. Earlier versions only warned and drew the model without the file; this is a deliberate change, because a picture drawn without a file it asked for would be silently wrong.

The warning for an href that was not drawn (missing, outside the folder, a network URL, a file type that is not listed here, a cycle, or a limit); it names the href and the reason, and --strict makes it an error.

The warning for an image whose picture is too large for the pixel budget of the render (64 million pixels in all, counted before anything is allocated, so a huge raster in a tiny box is refused, not decoded); nothing is drawn, and --strict makes it an error.

<image href="part.scad" x="10" y="10" width="120" height="120"/> draws the model part.scad, which sits beside the SVG file, in a 120 by 120 box. Print a whole diagram with: canvasnet help svg --example embed
These are silently not drawn, with no diagnostic: animation (animate and the rest of SMIL), foreignObject, nested svg elements, and filter primitives the library does not know.
A filter over its work budget is skipped: the element is drawn unfiltered.

Scripting, and image references the tool never follows: a network URL, an absolute path, and a path that leaves the folder of the SVG file (a symbolic link is refused too). Each is reported as svg-image-unresolved and not drawn.
A feImage filter primitive reads only a data: URI, never a file.

An embedded file is not shown with the options of the outer command: a model uses the view the library chooses for it (its own $vp* variables are honored, or the view= of its href), a document page is the one its href names (page 1 by default), and --page, --dpi, -D, and --param apply to the SVG file only (an embedded model or chart takes its values from the def. and param. parameters of its href).
At most 64 files are embedded in one render, SVG files nest 4 levels deep, an SVG file that embeds itself stops at once, and the pictures of one render may use at most 64 million pixels in all.
A malformed document, or one over a limit (5,000,000 characters, nesting depth 100, 100,000 rendered elements), is rejected as corrupt-input.
Draw at this width, keeping the aspect ratio; --height does the same for the height. The drawing is sharp, never enlarged afterwards.
Draw inside this box, centered and never stretched.
Multiply the intrinsic size by a factor.
The color transparency is flattened over (white by default); transparent keeps alpha.

An image that was not drawn (svg-image-unresolved, svg-image-too-large, image-fragment-invalid, or image-page-out-of-range) is an unsupported-feature error instead of a warning, and so is an unsupported feature of an embedded model or chart. The warnings image-fragment-unknown-parameter, image-fragment-duplicate-parameter, and vl-param-unknown stay warnings: the picture was drawn.

Warning: an image href was not drawn. The message names the href and why: not found, outside the folder, a network URL, a format the tool cannot draw, a cycle, or a limit. With --strict it is an unsupported-feature error.

Warning: an image was not drawn because its picture does not fit in the pixel budget of the render. The message names the href and the pixels it needs. With --strict it is an unsupported-feature error.

Warning: the fragment of an href names a parameter the linked file does not use (a typo such as pag=2, or any parameter on a raster or an SVG file). The picture is drawn without it. --strict does not fail on it.
Warning: the fragment gives a parameter twice with different values; the last one is used. --strict does not fail on it.
Warning: a param.<name> of the fragment names a param the chart does not declare (a typo, or a chart without params). The chart is drawn without it. --strict does not fail on it.

Unsupported: a value that is not allowed (page=0, page=abc, page=2.5, an empty value, an unknown view name, a def. value that is not valid JSON when it starts with [ or a name that is not an identifier, a param. value that is not valid JSON) or a fragment over its limit. The image is not drawn; with --strict it is an unsupported-feature error. For an input path of the command line the same mistake is an error with this code.
Unsupported: the page or slide does not exist (page=9 of a 2-page document). The image is not drawn and the message tells how many pages there are; with --strict it is an unsupported-feature error.
With --json each of these reports carries the embedding file in origin (see 'canvasnet help json'); the message starts with the href as written.
The notes of an embedded model, chart, or SVG file are reported too, each starting with the href of the file, and the lines an embedded model prints with echo are kept.
An embedded file that is found but is broken (a corrupt picture, a model with a syntax error, a chart with a bad specification) is an error with its own code, and the message names both files.
Error code: malformed XML, a root element that is not svg, or a document over a limit.
No scripting, animation, or network resources; images are read only from the folder of the SVG file, and only by the command line tool (the library opts in with SvgLoadOptions.ImageResolver).

Text is best effort without shaping. An installed family is used, so text can differ between machines; generic and unknown families use the bundled Liberation fonts. A character those lack (such as U+221D) is taken from the bundled Noto fonts; a character nothing covers draws the font's missing-glyph box with no diagnostic, because SVG rendering reports nothing.

Lengths: ex is the height of the font's x glyph and ch the advance of 0 (half an em when the font has no such glyph); a normal line height is 1.2 em; vw, vh, vmin, and vmax are percentages of the root viewport in user units (the viewBox, else the root width and height), which differs from a browser only when the two disagree; and percent in a gradient, pattern, or mask coordinate is a fraction of 1 under objectBoundingBox (the default) but is relative to the viewport (width for x, height for y, the diagonal for r) under userSpaceOnUse, the same for a plain percent and one inside calc(). The root width and height can use font-relative units (against the root's own font-size attribute or style), but a percent or viewport unit there is ignored. The keyword sizes follow the browsers' table, not the CSS Fonts factors (9.6, 12, 14.2, 16, 19.2, 24, 32, and 48).

A length that is not valid (an unknown unit, a space between number and unit, a bad calc(), a calc() that resolves to a plain number) in a shape, a text position, the stroke width, a dash pattern (stroke-dasharray), or a dash offset (stroke-dashoffset) is corrupt-input. In a gradient, pattern, or mask coordinate, or in the root width and height, it is ignored and the default is used; an invalid font-size, line-height, or font shorthand is ignored, so the size is inherited (a browser does the same).

Units are not converted for: letter-spacing, word-spacing, tspan positioning (x, y, dx, and dy on a tspan), the lists of dx and dy beyond the first value on a text element, textLength, baseline-shift, and nested svg elements (which are not drawn, so their width, height, x, and y are never read).
The drawing is rendered sharply at the target size, not rasterized first and scaled afterwards.
